MNIST Reader¶

In [2]:
# https://www.kaggle.com/code/hojjatk/read-mnist-dataset

#
# This is a sample Notebook to demonstrate how to read "MNIST Dataset"
#

import struct
from array import array

#
# MNIST Data Loader Class
#
class MnistDataloader(object):
    def __init__(self, training_images_filepath,training_labels_filepath, test_images_filepath, test_labels_filepath):
        self.training_images_filepath = training_images_filepath
        self.training_labels_filepath = training_labels_filepath
        self.test_images_filepath = test_images_filepath
        self.test_labels_filepath = test_labels_filepath
    
    def read_images_labels(self, images_filepath, labels_filepath):
        labels = []
        with open(labels_filepath, 'rb') as file:
            magic, size = struct.unpack(">II", file.read(8))
            if magic != 2049:
                raise ValueError('Magic number mismatch, expected 2049, got {}'.format(magic))
            labels = np.array(array("B", file.read())).reshape((-1, 1))
        
        with open(images_filepath, 'rb') as file:
            magic, size, rows, cols = struct.unpack(">IIII", file.read(16))
            if magic != 2051:
                raise ValueError('Magic number mismatch, expected 2051, got {}'.format(magic))
            image_data = array("B", file.read())
        images = []
        for i in range(size):
            images.append(None)
        for i in range(size):
            img = np.array(image_data[i * rows * cols:(i + 1) * rows * cols])
            img = img.reshape(28, 28)
            images[i] = img
        return np.array(images), labels
            
    def load_data(self):
        x_train, y_train = self.read_images_labels(self.training_images_filepath, self.training_labels_filepath)
        x_test, y_test = self.read_images_labels(self.test_images_filepath, self.test_labels_filepath)
        return (x_train, y_train),(x_test, y_test)

def show_images(images, labels, title, cmp_labels = None):
    num_showed_imgs_x = min(10, int(math.ceil(math.sqrt(len(labels)))))
    num_showed_imgs_y = min(10, int(math.ceil(math.sqrt(len(labels)))))

    figsize = (10, 10)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(num_showed_imgs_y, num_showed_imgs_x, figsize=figsize)
    fig.suptitle(title)
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.setp(plt.gcf().get_axes(), xticks=[], yticks=[])
    for i, ax in enumerate(axes.flat):
        if i >= len(images):
            break
        img = images[i]
        ax.imshow(img, cmap='gray')
        if cmp_labels is None:
            ax.set_title(f"{labels[i]}")
        else:
            ax.set_title(f"Actual: {labels[i]}\nGot: {cmp_labels[i]}")

MNIST Dataset Class¶

In [10]:
class MNISTDatasetLoader:
    def __init__(self, x: np.array, y: np.array, batch_size: int, clamp_x_0_1: bool = True, normalize_x: bool = True, flatten_x: bool = True, one_hot_y: bool = True, shuffle: bool = True):
        assert(len(x) == len(y))
        assert(batch_size > 0)
        self.x = np.copy(x)
        self.y = np.copy(y)
        if clamp_x_0_1:
            self.x = self.x.astype(np.float64) / 255.0
        if normalize_x:
            self.x = (self.x.astype(np.float64) - np.mean(self.x)) / np.std(self.x)
        if flatten_x:
            self.x = np.reshape(self.x, (-1, self.x.shape[1] * self.x.shape[2]))
        if one_hot_y:
            self.y = np.zeros((len(y), 10)).astype(np.float64)
            self.y[np.arange(len(y)), y.ravel()] = np.float64(1.0)
        self.batch_size = batch_size
        self._ptr = 0
        self._perm = None
        self.shuffle = shuffle
    def __iter__(self):
        self._ptr = 0
        self._perm = np.random.permutation(len(self.x)) if self.shuffle else None
        return self
    def __next__(self):
        if self._ptr >= len(self.x):
            raise StopIteration
        end = min(self._ptr + self.batch_size, len(self.x))
        idx = self._perm[self._ptr:end] if self._perm is not None else slice(self._ptr, end)
        self._ptr = end
        return self.x[idx], self.y[idx]
    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.x)
    def __getitem__(self, i):
        return self.x[i], self.y[i]
    def get_x(self):
        return self.x
    def get_y(self):
        return self.y
    def get_batch(self, i):
        if i >= len(self.x):
            raise IndexError("Out of range")
        end = min(i + self.batch_size, len(self.x))
        return self.x[i:end], self.y[i:end]

Helpers¶

In [12]:
def softmax(x, dim=None):
    e_x = np.exp(x - x.max(axis=dim, keepdims=True))
    return e_x / e_x.sum(axis=dim, keepdims=True)

Network Class¶

In [13]:
class MNISTNN:
    def __init__(self, params):
        self.w1 = np.random.randn(params["w_h"], params["s"]) * np.sqrt(2.0 / params["w_h"]).astype(np.float64)
        self.b1 = np.zeros((1, params["s"])).astype(np.float64)
        self.w2 = np.random.randn(params["s"], params["k"]) * np.sqrt(2.0 / params["s"]).astype(np.float64)
        self.b2 = np.zeros((1, params["k"])).astype(np.float64)
        self.lr = np.float64(params["lr"])

    def forward(self, x):
        self.z1 = np.dot(x, self.w1) + self.b1
        self.a1 = np.maximum(0, self.z1)
        self.z2 = np.dot(self.a1, self.w2) + self.b2
        self.p = softmax(self.z2, dim=1)
        return self.p

    def backward(self, x, y):
        dz2 = (self.p - y) / x.shape[0]

        self.dw2 = np.dot(self.a1.T, dz2)
        self.db2 = dz2.sum(axis=0, keepdims=True)

        da1 = np.dot(dz2, self.w2.T)
        dz1 = da1 * (self.z1 > 0).astype(np.float64)

        self.dw1 = np.dot(x.T, dz1)
        self.db1 = dz1.sum(axis=0, keepdims=True)

    def step(self):
        self.w1 -= self.lr * self.dw1
        self.b1 -= self.lr * self.db1
        self.w2 -= self.lr * self.dw2
        self.b2 -= self.lr * self.db2

Train and test¶

In [14]:
def train(model, train_loader, epoch):
    tp = 0
    n = 0
    t_start = time.time()
    for i, (images, labels) in enumerate(train_loader):
        outputs = model.forward(images)
        model.backward(images, labels)
        model.step()
        tp += (outputs.argmax(axis=1) == labels.argmax(axis=1)).sum()
        n += len(images)
    elapsed = time.time() - t_start
    acc = tp / n
    print(f"TRAIN Epoch {epoch}, train acc: {acc}, train err: {1.0 - acc}, train time: {elapsed}")
    return (acc, elapsed)
def test(model, test_loader, epoch):
    tp = 0
    n = 0
    for i, (images, labels) in enumerate(test_loader):
        outputs = model.forward(images)
        tp += (outputs.argmax(axis=1) == labels.argmax(axis=1)).sum()
        n += len(labels)
    acc = tp / n
    print(f"TEST Epoch {epoch}, test acc: {acc}, test err: {1.0 - acc}")
    return acc

PyTorch test¶

In [16]:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
import torch.optim as optim
from torchvision import datasets, transforms

class torchNET(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, params):
        super(torchNET, self).__init__()
        self.layers = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Flatten(1, -1),
            nn.Linear(params["w_h"], params["s"]),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(params["s"], params["k"]),
            #nn.Softmax(dim=1) # exclude if `loss_func = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()`
        )
    def forward(self, x):
        return self.layers(x)

def torch_train(model, train_loader, optimizer, loss_func, epoch):
    model.train()
    tp = 0
    n = 0
    t_start = time.time()
    for i, (images, labels) in enumerate(train_loader):
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        outputs = model(images)
        loss = loss_func(outputs, labels)
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        tp += (outputs.argmax(dim=1) == labels).sum()
        n += labels.size(0)
    elapsed = time.time() - t_start
    acc = tp / n
    print(f"TRAIN Epoch {epoch}, train acc: {acc}, train err: {1.0 - acc} train time: {elapsed}")
    return (acc, elapsed)

def torch_test(model, test_loader, epoch):
    model.eval()
    tp = 0
    n = 0
    with torch.no_grad():
        for i, (images, labels) in enumerate(test_loader):
            outputs = model(images)
            tp += (outputs.argmax(dim=1) == labels).sum()
            n += labels.size(0)
    acc = tp / n
    print(f"TEST Epoch {epoch}, test acc: {acc}, test err: {1.0 - acc}")
    return acc

pytorch_res = {
    "train_acc": [],
    "train_time": [],
    "test_acc": []
}
if True:
    transform = transforms.Compose([
        transforms.ToTensor(),
        transforms.Normalize((0.1307,), (0.3081,))
    ])
    dataset1 = datasets.MNIST('./MNIST_PYTORCH', train=True, download=True, transform=transform)
    dataset2 = datasets.MNIST('./MNIST_PYTORCH', train=False, transform=transform)
    with open("./MNIST_PYTORCH/.gitignore", "w") as f:
        f.write("*\n")
    train_loader = torch.utils.data.DataLoader(dataset1, batch_size=task_params["batch_size"])
    test_loader = torch.utils.data.DataLoader(dataset2, batch_size=task_params["batch_size"])
    model = torchNET(task_params)
    optimizer = optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=task_params["lr"])
    #loss_func = nn.NLLLoss() # include `nn.Softmax(dim=1)` in model
    loss_func = nn.CrossEntropyLoss() # exclude `nn.Softmax(dim=1)` in model
    for epoch in range(task_params["epochs"]):
        train_acc, train_time = torch_train(model, train_loader, optimizer, loss_func, epoch)
        test_acc = torch_test(model, test_loader, epoch)
        pytorch_res["train_acc"].append(train_acc)
        pytorch_res["train_time"].append(train_time)
        pytorch_res["test_acc"].append(test_acc)
    train_acc = np.array(pytorch_res["train_acc"])
    train_time = np.array(pytorch_res["train_time"])
    test_acc = np.array(pytorch_res["test_acc"])
    train_err = -train_acc + 1.0
    test_err = -test_acc + 1.0
    print(f"TRAIN avg train acc: {train_acc.mean()}, avg train err: {train_err.mean()}, avg train time: {train_time.mean()}")
    print(f"TEST avg test acc: {test_acc.mean()}, avg test_err {test_err.mean()}")
    # Save numpy
    pytorch_res["train_acc"] = train_acc
    pytorch_res["train_time"] = train_time
    pytorch_res["test_acc"] = test_acc
    # Some test results
    images, labels = next(iter(test_loader))
    outputs = model.forward(images)
    show_images(images.reshape((len(images), 28, 28)), labels, "Some test results", outputs.argmax(axis=1))

def two_curves_plot(x_1, y_1, x_2, y_2, label_1, label_2, title):
    plt.plot(x_1, y_1, label=label_1)
    plt.plot(x_2, y_2, label=label_2)
    plt.title(title)
    plt.legend()
    plt.show()
